start.title: The Voice from Above
start.text:
God speaks to you.
"Make yourself an ark. A flood is coming."

choices.text: Receive God's command to build an ark of cypress wood
choices.feedback: Genesis 6:14, 22 — God told Noah to make an ark of cypress wood, and Noah did everything just as God commanded.

choices.text: Refuse the command and flee the land
choices.feedback: Genesis says Noah obeyed God; he did not flee.

choices.text: Buy an existing ship from a merchant
choices.feedback: Genesis says Noah built the ark himself, as God instructed.

mockery.title: A Watching World
mockery.text:
The world around you is corrupt and violent.
They watch you build. How do you respond?

choices.text: Keep building the ark by faith
choices.feedback: Hebrews 11:7 — By faith Noah built the ark in reverent fear, though warned of things not yet seen.

choices.text: Abandon the ark to please the crowd
choices.feedback: Scripture says Noah kept building by faith.

choices.text: Attack the mockers to silence them
choices.feedback: Scripture does not describe Noah attacking anyone.

building.title: Cypress and Pitch
building.text:
You gather the materials God commanded.
How do you build the ark?

choices.text: Build it of cypress wood, coated with pitch inside and out
choices.feedback: Genesis 6:14 — Make yourself an ark of cypress wood; coat it with pitch inside and out.

choices.text: Build it from cut stone
choices.feedback: Genesis says the ark was built of cypress wood, not stone.

choices.text: Weave it from reeds like a basket
choices.feedback: Genesis says the ark was made of cypress wood, sealed with pitch.

ark_done.title: It Stands Finished
ark_done.text:
The ark is complete, exactly as God commanded.
What does it look like?

choices.text: 300 cubits long, 50 wide, 30 high, with three decks
choices.feedback: Genesis 6:15-16 — The ark was 300 cubits long, 50 wide, 30 high, with three decks.

choices.text: A small round boat with one deck
choices.feedback: Genesis gives specific dimensions; the ark was not a small round boat.

choices.text: A raft, flat and open to the sky
choices.feedback: Genesis says the ark had a roof, three decks, and a door in its side.

animals.title: The Creatures Come
animals.text:
The animals arrive at the ark.
Who do you take on board?

choices.text: Take pairs of every kind of animal, male and female
choices.feedback: Genesis 7:8-9 — Pairs of clean and unclean animals, birds and creeping things came to Noah, male and female.

choices.text: Take only sheep and goats
choices.feedback: Genesis says every kind of animal came, not only sheep and goats.

choices.text: Take no animals — only your family
choices.feedback: Genesis says the animals came into the ark with Noah.

boarding.title: The Door Shut
boarding.text:
It is time to enter the ark.
Who enters, and who closes the door?

choices.text: Enter with your wife, three sons, and their wives; the Lord shuts the door
choices.feedback: Genesis 7:13, 16 — Noah, his wife, his three sons and their wives entered the ark, and the Lord shut him in.

choices.text: Enter the ark alone, leaving your family behind
choices.feedback: Genesis says Noah's whole household entered the ark with him.

choices.text: Stay outside and close the door from without
choices.feedback: Genesis says the Lord Himself shut Noah inside the ark.

storm.title: Forty Days of Rain
storm.text:
The windows of heaven open.
What happens?

choices.text: Rain falls on the earth for forty days and forty nights
choices.feedback: Genesis 7:12 — Rain fell on the earth forty days and forty nights.

choices.text: A single storm passes in one day
choices.feedback: Genesis says the rain fell for forty days and nights.

choices.text: Only a light drizzle falls
choices.feedback: Genesis describes the fountains of the deep bursting and the windows of heaven opening.

inside.title: Upon the Waters
inside.text:
The ark floats on the deep.
How long do the waters prevail on the earth?

choices.text: The waters flood the earth for a hundred and fifty days
choices.feedback: Genesis 7:24 — The waters flooded the earth for a hundred and fifty days.

choices.text: The waters recede in three days
choices.feedback: Genesis says the waters prevailed 150 days before receding.

choices.text: You steer the ark back toward Eden
choices.feedback: Genesis does not describe Noah steering the ark; God kept it afloat.

dove.title: The Dove Returns
dove.text:
The waters begin to recede.
How do you know dry land is near?

choices.text: Send out a dove; it returns with a fresh olive leaf
choices.feedback: Genesis 8:11 — The dove returned to Noah in the evening with a freshly plucked olive leaf.

choices.text: Send out a raven that returns with grain
choices.feedback: Genesis says the dove — not the raven — brought back an olive leaf.

choices.text: Open the roof and look with your own eyes only
choices.feedback: Genesis says Noah sent out birds to test whether the waters had gone down.

dry_land.title: Earth Beneath Your Feet
dry_land.text:
The Lord tells you to come out of the ark.
What do you do first on dry land?

choices.text: Build an altar to the Lord and offer sacrifices
choices.feedback: Genesis 8:20 — Noah built an altar to the Lord and offered burnt offerings on it.

choices.text: Begin building a great tower right away
choices.feedback: Genesis says Noah's first act was to build an altar, not a tower.

choices.text: Refuse to leave the ark
choices.feedback: Genesis says Noah came out of the ark when God told him to.

covenant.title: The Rainbow
covenant.text:
A rainbow arches across the sky.
"Never again will I flood the earth. This is my covenant with you."
